newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Delta and BHP see July Zimbabwe platinum start.
newsitem.headline: Delta and BHP see July Zimbabwe platinum start.

text.p: Zimbabwe's largest mining investment group Hartley Platinum mine will start hot commissioning of its base metal refinery in May, setting it on track for its first platinum production in July, a top mine official said on Tuesday.
"Hot commissioning of the base metal refinery is to start in May. I think we will see first production in July," Hartley Platinum mine general manager Colin Palethorpe told Reuters.

The mine, a joint venture between Australian mining giant Broken Hill Proprietary Ltd and Delta Gold NL, was originally forecast to start production at the end of 1996 but heavy rains, problems in breaking ground and training workers delayed the startup.
Palethorpe said the delays had pushed up the the costs of the project slightly to an estimated $289 million from $287 million.
"Training of miners is still our main area of concern because many of the workers have never worked in a mine before," he said.

The project is currently mining 27,000 tonnes of ore per month and aims to reach full production of 180,000 tonnes of ore by September 1998 when it is expected to have platinum output of 150,000 ounces, 110,000 ounces of palladium, 11,500 ounces of rhodium and 23,000 ounces of gold.
The project has so far employed 2,800 people and is looking at taking 300 more onto its books.
Palethorpe said the mine was having a few "teething problems" with the smelter but these were being sorted out and the smelter was in production.
